lesson: One add_load per load name with a types list covers a load shared by several car types; 32 actions covered 39 type/load pairs
Check numeric settings such as scale against the plan diff, not the name you typed
A blank railroad's first plan necessarily carries load-no-train and load-no-track errors; accept exactly those names and clear them in stage 3
Pass ops_dir on every plugin call; nothing sets OPS_DIR in a subagent's environment
Build a spur and its schedule in one plan (add_industry), since hold_custom and the other schedule options are refused on a bare spur
Read every plan diff before applying: a field value the plugin does not understand can be dropped silently
Order the build so engines exist before trains name a road or model, or set them afterwards with update_train
Give spurs unique names across industries, or create the schedule under its own name before the track; add_industry reuses a schedule whose name matches
A schedule whose lines point at a track that has no schedule yet still applies; cross-references between the two offline spurs need no ordering
update_car works inside an ops_plan after the add_car for the same car, so a car and its load go in one plan
Passenger types with no track raise type-no-track errors; cars that stay unplaced need accept_new_errors or a track that takes their type
To deliver a car onto a spur, give it the load the schedule line receives (usually E), not the load it carried in the old system; match mode refuses a car no line receives
Check each delivered car's type against the spur's type list before the plan; the tool reports the mismatch only at delivery
A dry run answers gate and routing questions, not session-order questions; to prove a hand-off, run an ordered automation on the copy
Ask ops_why_not one car and one train at a time and read first_failure and router; the gate list is for the diagnoser
Clear a startup automation with an empty string; name the railroad per train with set_train_manifest when the file has no railroad element
ops_dry_run cannot prove a session order; keep a replay automation for the live lane and test the hand-off on a running JMRI
JMRI sets default-load cars straight out on an alternate track; give alternates a load filter that excludes E and L
The custom-load search ignores final destinations it has not got: a loaded car placed without one goes to the receiving spur with the fewest moves, so give catch-all spurs a high move count
To change a train's route when an automation names one of its stops, replace the automation's steps, set the route, then put the steps back, all in one plan
Chain the plugin's JMRI worker (build, terminate, save, keep) to test a session order on copies; five jobs took under four minutes
